evals.prompt: Make me a 10-slide investor pitch deck about Flux — the event graph. I want it to look agency-grade but every chart editable.
evals.expected_output: A .pptx with cover → problem → bento_features → matrix_2x2 → stats_grid → timeline → bento_features → bar_chart (native c:chart) → quote → bar_chart with insight. All shapes native, no raster chart, theme vc_clean, 16:9 13.33x7.5, Bento 12-col grid. Passes validate_pptx.py --strict (no overlap, no overflow, no slop).
expectations: Produces a .pptx with 8-12 slides, at least one bento_features, one stats_grid, one matrix_2x2, and one native bar_chart
All charts are native c:chart (not p:pic screenshot) — editable data
No overlapping shapes (x2 - x > tolerance triggers fail)
Style derived per deck (vc_clean), not fixed 26-style clone — theme recolor preserved via schemeClr where templated
Passes scripts/validate_pptx.py --strict

evals.prompt: I have a branded template.pptx — use its masters to build a Q4 board report deck. Don't break the theme.
evals.expected_output: Profiles template.pptx to layout-catalog.md + config.json with [HINT: layout] names, maps each slide to a real placeholder via ph idx, fills placeholders via raw _element (not overlay), preserves a:schemeClr. No srgbClr hard-code where accent1 expected. Passes --check-theme.
expectations: Emits layout-catalog.md and config.json listing real layout names + placeholder idx/type/bounds
slides.md or spec uses [HINT: layout] that exists in config.json — linted
Content placed in placeholder (ph) via _element, not textbox overlay
No rasterized slides — all shapes remain vector
Passes validate_pptx.py --check-theme

evals.prompt: Create a dense academic deck from a paper — cover, method diagram, results table, bar chart, references. No filler.
evals.expected_output: A .pptx with academic_minimal theme (serif where editorial), method_diagram via native shapes/arrows (not Gemini hallucinated image), results_table as native table (banded, header schemeClr fill), bar_chart native, references with hanging indent via a:pPr marL/indent. Ghost-deck titles tell the story.
expectations: Uses academic_minimal palette + Georgia serif where appropriate
method_diagram is vector boxes+arrows, not generated PNG
results_table is native table (not screenshot)
Titles alone tell the argument (ghost-deck test)
Passes --strict with no slop/placeholder residue

evals.prompt: Build a Bento showcase deck — one slide per Bento layout. Prove no overlap.
evals.expected_output: 7+ slide deck covering Single Focus / 50-50 / Asymmetric 7+5 / Three-col 4+4+4 / Primary-Secondary 8+4 / Hero+Subs / Mixed Grid. Each card snaps to 12-col grid + GUTTER=0.32″, CARD_PAD=0.28″, bounds validated. No shape overflows canvas, no 2.5″ narrow body textbox, no overlapping.
expectations: Contains at least 5 distinct Bento layouts (Bento Grid palette not prison, but proves variety)
Every card satisfies left+width ≤ SLIDE_WIDTH-MARGIN and left ≥ MARGIN — validated via a:xfrm cx/cy
No two cards on same slide share identical span back-to-back without density alternation note
All text boxes have wordWrap=True, autoSize=None, width ≥2.5″ for body
Passes validate_pptx.py --check-overlap --check-overflow

evals.prompt: Generate a PPTX via the fast JS lane (PptxGenJS) for the same pitch — I need it in under 2 seconds.
evals.expected_output: Via scripts/render_pptx.mjs (Node, pptxgenjs) using same tokens/palette as Python — output is valid .pptx with editable shapes, same theme_key, geometry-clean. JS lane respects Bento tokens; not a pixel-dumped PNG deck.
expectations: Produces .pptx via PptxGenJS (npm install pptxgenjs) — not python-pptx
Same theme_key palette (BG/FG/ACCENT) shared with Python path — recolor consistent
All slides are editable shapes (no single p:pic ≥90% slide)
Passes validate_pptx.py --check-editable
Render completes without requiring LibreOffice
